correctness.rationale: For every permutation size of at least two, swapping an unordered pair of values at fixed sites produces a footrule difference equal to twice an integer interval-overlap count; this proves the exact cross-covariance. Three-point comparisons give the full positive-definite incidence covariance. The computed cross-covariance is a complete-graph cut vector and is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \((n+1)/12\), so the normal equations have exactly one solution. Double-centering the absolute-distance assignment matrix and polynomial power sums prove the exact variance and squared-coefficient norm, whence the optimal explained-variance fraction formula and the residual. The difference polynomial from the proof is negative at sizes two and three and positive for sizes at least four, proving the unique size-four minimum and limit. The packaged exact verifier passed 1,004 finite-enumeration assertions and 396 finite rational-polynomial checks. Those calculations are not relied upon as an all-size proof.

value.rationale: Spearman footrule measures positional ranking distortion while pairwise inversions encode Kendall-type disagreement. Their optimal linear relationship is a natural rank-association inference question. This theorem gives all predictor coefficients, a unique optimal projection, a universal sharp explained-variance bound of at least \(58/65\) (unique four-item worst case), and the nonzero \(5/56\) asymptotic residual. It quantifies precisely the linear surrogate adequacy and what remains nonlinear, beyond marginal-moment or scalar-covariance observations.
